 November 17, 2026 | Men's Basketball
 Share: UW opens tournament vs. Seton Hall on Thursday
 MADISON, Wis. —   The Wisconsin men’s basketball team will hit the road for the first time this season as it travels to Nassau, Bahamas to play Seton Hall for the first of two games of the Baha Mar Championship. Tip for the Bahamas is set for 7:30 p.m. CT. 
 Thursday’s game will air live on CBS Sports Network. Fans can also listen to the Badger Radio Network as Lane Grindle and Badger legend Brian Butch will be on the mic. 
 Fans on Thursday can meet up with other Badger fans at Vibe BBQ, located at the Grand Hyatt Baha Mar, starting at 6:30 p.m. ET (food and drinks will be available for purchase). 
 UW will take on either N.C. State or Murray State on Friday in the final day of the Baha Mar Championship. The consolation game starts at 6 p.m. CT while the championship game will begin at 8:30 p.m. CT. Both games will air on CBS Sports Network.  
 Prior to the game on Friday, a Badger Fan Event will be hosted on the Jasmine Lawn outside of the  Baha Mar Convention Center at a time to be determined. 
 Nolan Winter had 14 points and 9 boards vs. Coastal Carolina LAST TIME OUT
 The men’s basketball team defeated Coastal Carolina, 89-81, on Sunday at the Kohl Center. Owen Foxwell provided the offensive firepower for Wisconsin (4-0), leading the team with 33 points and 6 assists in the high-scoring affair. Nolan Winter was an offensive force as well, scoring 14 points and grabbing 9 rebounds, 7 of which were on the offensive side of the ball. Will Garlock had a standout performance, tallying 3 points and 10 rebounds off the bench. Wisconsin’s 51-point second half effort was enough to capture the victory for the Cardinal and White. 
 A night to remember from Foxwell https://t.co/O6sC3LuBx2
— Wisconsin Basketball (@BadgerMBB) November 16, 2026 FOXWELL ON FIRE
 Owen Foxwell has been off to an excellent start to his career for the Badgers, averaging 19.25 points per game and 5.5 assists through the first four contests. Foxwell had his best night of the season Sunday against the Chanticleers, with his 33 points being the highest of any freshman in UW history since at least 1990. The savvy point guard took over the game in the second half, scoring 27 points—the most by a Badger in the second half this season. For his efforts, Foxwell was named the Big Ten Freshman of the Week. 
 NOVEMBER SUCCESS
 UW is looking for its 4th holiday tournament title in the last 6 seasons after winning the 2021 Maui Invitational, the 2023 Fort Myers Tip-Off & the 2024 Greenbrier Tip-Off. The Badgers have won 10 of their last 12 November tournament games. 
 Chucky Hepburn helped UW to a third-place showing in the Battle 4 Atlantis in 2022 BACK TO THE BAHAMAS 
 The last time the Badgers played in the Bahamas was the 2022-23 season, in the Battle 4 Atlantis. Wisconsin opened the tournament with a 43-42 win over Dayton, led by the 13-points career high from Connor Essegian. The Badgers lost a tight game with No. 3 Kansas 68-69, before turning it around to defeat USC 64-59, led by the 17-point performance from Chucky Hepburn and a solid 14-point outing from Tyler Wahl. Wisconsin will look to improve on this performance this year as they return to the Bahamas. 
 AGAINST THE PIRATES
 The Wisconsin men’s team has never faced off against the Pirates in program history. This season, Seton Hall sits at 3-1 with its only loss coming against No. 18 Alabama. The Pirates fell short 81-76, with Ilay Dolinsky scoring 15 points off the bench. Seton Hall is averaging 69.1 points per game this season, compared to UW’s 81.5.
